# Move-Out Cleaning Checklist for Cape Town Tenants

Moving is expensive enough without **deposit surprises**. This guide is **transactional checklist authority** for **tenants** preparing a **handover-ready** home in Cape Town: kitchens, bathrooms, cupboards, walls, and the “estate agent glance.” It complements [**what is included in deep cleaning**](https://shalean.co.za/blog/whats-included-in-deep-cleaning-cape-town) for **service scope**, but it is written for **lease exit outcomes**—not weekly maintenance psychology.

---

## Quick answer: what landlords and agents actually scan first

**Kitchens and bathrooms** carry disproportionate deposit risk because soil is obvious under bright light. Next: **floors**, **cupboard faces**, **windows and tracks**, and **walls** at child-height and behind furniture.

---

## Kitchen checklist (high yield)

- Degrease hob, backsplash, and cupboard fronts you touched daily
- Clean inside microwave; **oven interior** if your lease requires it (often an add-on—confirm booking line items)
- Sink, taps, and drain smell (run hot water; check trap if instructed by landlord)
- Empty all cupboards; wipe shelves; remove stickers and shelf liners if required
- Fridge/freezer: empty, wipe, leave off with doors ajar **only if** your lease requires it

---

## Bathroom checklist (high yield)

- Limescale on taps, shower screens, and tracks
- Toilet bowl, seat hinges, and pedestal behind
- Mirrors polished without streak “halo”
- Extractor fan grille dust
- Floor corners and silicone lines

---

## Bedrooms and living areas

- Skirting and door frames where dust lines show after furniture moves
- Built-in cupboard tracks and shelves emptied and wiped
- Cobwebs in corners and ceiling lines
- Light switches and handles (high-touch film)

---

## Walls, marks, and “fair wear and tear”

**Small scuffs** sometimes wipe; **deep paint damage** is not “cleaning” in the bond sense—document photos early. If walls are genuinely marked, align with your landlord before spending on the wrong fix.

---

## Estate agents and inspection lighting

Agents often inspect with **side light** and **open blinds**—the same tricks that make a home photograph well. Walk the unit twice: once overhead, once with **critical light** on wet rooms.

---

## Booking professional help for move-out

If time is tight, book **deep-scoped** cleaning with explicit **add-ons** that match your lease (oven/fridge/walls if required). Compare [**deep cleaning Cape Town**](https://shalean.co.za/services/deep-cleaning-cape-town) line items and [**pricing**](https://shalean.co.za/cleaning-prices-cape-town) before checkout—not a vague “full clean.”

### Mid-article CTA

Use this checklist room-by-room, then translate it into **booking ticks**: [**deep vs standard**](https://shalean.co.za/blog/deep-vs-standard-cleaning-which-to-book-cape-town) for tier, [**scope checklist**](https://shalean.co.za/blog/whats-included-in-deep-cleaning-cape-town) for depth, [**same-day**](https://shalean.co.za/blog/same-day-cleaning-cape-town) only if routing still allows.

---

## Cupboards, shelves, and “empty enough”

Agents often open cupboards. **Empty** means no stray packets, no sticky rings, and no dust lines on shelves you forgot existed. If you half-empty cupboards, you half-pass inspection.

---

## Windows, tracks, and balcony doors

Tracks collect grit that reads as neglect under inspection light. A pass on glass without tracks can still fail the **estate glance** test.

---

## Documentation that protects your deposit

Photo the oven, fridge, and bathrooms **before** and **after** your final clean. If there is a dispute, timestamps and line-item scope beat memory.

---

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need professional cleaning to get my deposit back?

Not always legally required, but it is often the **fastest** way to meet inspection standards—especially kitchens and baths.

### Should I book deep cleaning for move-out?

Usually **yes** when the lease expects **inspection-grade** wet rooms and edges—confirm line items.

### Are ovens and fridges included?

Only if **scoped**—confirm add-ons at booking.

### What if my lease lists “carpets professionally cleaned”?

That may require **specialist carpet** services outside standard residential scope—read your lease literally.

### Can cleaners remove wall scuffs?

**Surface** marks sometimes; **paint damage** may need touch-ups.

---

## Balconies, garages, and “not really inside” zones

Some leases include outdoor storage or balcony glass. If it is in your inventory photos, assume it is in scope mentally—even if you wish it were not.

---

## Keys, alarms, and final walkthrough etiquette

If you arm an alarm after cleaning, confirm codes with the agent. A last-minute lockout wastes the clean window and creates avoidable stress.

---

## If the agent requests a touch-up

Touch-ups are normal. A scoped **small return visit** beats arguing from memory—keep photos and line items aligned with what was booked.

---

## Light fittings and overlooked dust traps

Ceiling fittings and tops of door frames collect dust that shows in inspection photos. A quick pass on reachable fixtures is high yield when time is tight.

---

## Final mindset: “inventory photography,” not “my normal tidy”

Handover is judged like a product photo: harsh light, open cupboards, and zoomed context. Clean for that lens—not for how the home felt on a Tuesday evening.

---

## End CTA

Turn checklist into scope: book [**deep cleaning Cape Town**](https://shalean.co.za/services/deep-cleaning-cape-town) with the add-ons your lease demands, verify totals on [**cleaning prices**](https://shalean.co.za/cleaning-prices-cape-town), and hand over keys with **photo evidence** and a clean paper trail.
